name: Calendar, full access
plain: Reads and edits every event in the person's calendars.
meaning: Calendars show meetings, attendees, travel, doctor visits and routines.

android.persistence: Until revoked; auto-reset after months unused

ios.note: requestAccess(to:) is deprecated in iOS 17; read and write are split

limits.headline: Can see, add and change every event in all your calendars once you allow full access
limits.user_action: You tap Allow Full Access when the app asks about your calendar
can: Change or delete events that already exist
Check your calendar again later without asking each time
cannot: Reach any event before you tap Allow Full Access
Use the old single request on iPhone; iOS 17 split it
Keep access after you turn it off in Settings
limits.differs: iPhone shows Allow Full Access or Don't Allow; Android shows Allow or Don't allow.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app read and change every event in all your calendars.
story.for_you: The prompt says the app wants full access to your calendar. If you allow it, the app can see meetings, locations and guests, and edit or delete them.
story.for_makers: Full access lets a smart assistant plan your day, find clashes and join calls. It is powerful and sensitive, since the calendar shows where you are, who you meet and your appointments.

use_cases.example: A meeting assistant joins your calls and writes notes from your calendar.
A day planner shows calendar and tasks in one view.
A travel app finds flights that fit between meetings.
A wellness app finds time for breaks.
A work tool measures how much time you spend in meetings.
A sales app logs customer meetings automatically.
An ad SDK could read events to guess interests, which store policies forbid.

risks: Reveals where you are and who you meet
story.android_note: Android has a calendar permission group for read and write.
story.ios_note: iOS 17 split read and write, and the older request call is deprecated.

technical_bounds: iOS 17 and later require the new keys; old key stops working for new targets

history.change: Full access key and write-only option introduced
